runs.content: Sunday's rotation picks whichever domain has gone longest without a deep-dive — Work qualified (only 2 pages, unchanged since 2026-05-15, never previously given a dedicated Sunday focus while Games got 09-13 and Lightfin got 09-06). Deep-read work/overview.md and work/source-workday-disruption-debate-2026.md in full: every substantive cross-domain link the debate supports (Mobley v. Workday discrimination suit, the ABN framework, Dwarkesh's Agent Civilizations incident, idea-wday.md's short-research gap) has already been made in prior runs, and no new Work material has arrived since May — so the domain itself yielded nothing new today. Instead, reconciling today's own Finance log entries surfaced a real pipeline-diagnosis error: finance/models/model-portfolio-management.md's strategy-feedback-loop review flags the Turso 'signals' table's Magic Formula rows as 10 days stale and asks whether the screening job has stopped firing — but log.md shows an mf-update job ran the same day with a Top 3 (MGNS/DNLM/GSK) identical to 2026-09-13's. Checking scheduled-task configs outside the wiki (portfolio-management-briefing/SKILL.md) explains why both are true: there are three separate, redundant Magic Formula computations (mf-update's own small-universe scrape, the full ~1,350-ticker Turso universe, and a third path in market-watchlist-tracker), and the SKILL.md already notes mf-update 'hasn't been retired... flagged separately for Mike to decide.' The small-universe job never stopped — it's the larger Turso-universe screen that's actually stalled, and nothing in the wiki records that these are different jobs. Concrete next step: add a note to model-portfolio-management.md naming the three-pipeline split so future stale-screen diagnoses point at the right job. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-19.

Saturday's rotation is a full sweep — skim every domain's overview/index page instead of deep-reading one, biasing toward cross-domain connections over investigation ideas. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-18, Thursday), the wiki was quiet: log.md shows exactly one new item — a podcast-summarizer run today created podcasts/podcast-dividend-talk-art-of-the-turnaround.md, a retrospective episode built entirely around 'what separates a genuine turnaround from a value trap' and position sizing when a dividend payer is under stress. That single new page produced one connection and no new investigation ideas (nothing else changed this week to surface anything new). Cross-domain connection: the episode's turnaround-vs-value-trap framework lands directly on finance/investor-letters/source-burry-build-a-bear-part1-2026-08-29.md — Burry's live, unresolved Build-A-Bear (BBW) long, which shows exactly the diagnostic signals the episode teaches in the abstract (no kitchen-sink impairment/write-down despite the earnings miss, a new CEO reversing the specific 'plushy push' brand-dilution mistake that caused the stumble, growth capex raised not cut) while Burry himself is explicitly 'no rush to add; awaiting the 10-Q' before Part 2's valuation verdict. BBW isn't a dividend payer, so this sharpens rather than directly extends the episode's own dividend-growth frame, but neither page cross-links the other despite describing the same judgment call. Concrete next step: once Fred listens, add a line to the Burry source page's See Also citing the episode's framework as a lens for the pending Part 2 verdict.
